claims.hypothesis: Is there a compact Hot Core component with very high water abundance and HDO fractionation?
claims.experiment: Radiative transfer modeling of HIFI H2(18)O, HD18O lines plus ALMA HDO maps
claims.finding: Water is recently evaporated ice mantle material in a small clump south of the continuum peak

evidence.quote: well modeled as emitting from a small ($\sim 2''$) clump with a high abundance of H$_2$O ($\chi = 6.5 \times 10^{-4}$ relative to H$_2$) and a HDO/H$_2$O ratio of 0.003.

claims.hypothesis: Does the outflow have different deuteration from compact components?
claims.experiment: Column densities of emission and absorption components
claims.result: Outflow HDO/H2O lower, absorption component lowest
claims.finding: Gas-phase shock chemistry may modify the ratio

evidence.quote: The outflowing gas, observed with both emission and absorption components, has a lower HDO/H$_2$O ratio than the compact components in Orion KL

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Observed continuum with higher density (1e9 cm-3) fits HDO equally well as enhanced continuum

evidence.quote: If the observed continuum is used instead, an equally good fit can be obtained with a higher H$_2$ density ($10^9$ cm$^{-3}$)

limitations_admitted.value: ALMA data lack zero-spacing; HDO collision rates only up to 450 K so highest HDO lines cannot be modeled; vibrational pumping excluded

evidence.quote: The ALMA observation was performed without zero-spacing information.
At the present time, therefore, we cannot model the highest-energy transitions of HDO detected by HIFI.
